newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Capel B&K keeps India Crompton buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Capel B&K keeps India Crompton buy.

text.p: Securities firm James Capel B&K on Tuesday maintained its "buy" recommendation on electrical equipment maker Crompton Greaves after the firm announced a drop in net profit for 1996/97 (April-March).
The firm said its net dropped sharply to 307.6 million rupees during the financial year ended March 31, 1997, from 640.4 million a year earlier.
Crompton's results fell below market expectations, and shares of the firm dropped 8.0 rupees, or 10.0 percent to 72.25 on the Bombay bourse.

"Sales growth has been flat, operating margins have contracted, interest costs have gone up substantially, and other income has declined," Capel B&K analyst Prabodh Agarwal said in a note to investors.
"Consequently net profit has nosedived by 52 percent."
Agarwal said sales growth had fallen four percent during the second half of 1996/97 due to an industrial slowdown and a liquidity crunch, but added that 1997/98 would be a year of consolidation.
"Better outlook on economic and industrial growth would result in moderate topline growth, slight expansion in operating margins, and lower interest costs," he said.
He said there was likely to be significant growth in the 1998/99 fiscal year when the full impact of expected higher industrial growth would be felt.
"The worst seems to be over for the company, and we continue to recommend a buy on the scrip, in view of its attractive valuation."
Agarwal said Crompton shares had underperformed Bombay's benchmark stocks index by some 20 percent in the past one month and by 30 percent in the past three months.
"It is currently trading at 1996/97 price to cash flow per share of 5.8 times and a price to book value of 0.75 times," he said.
